monologue: The card hums warm under me, a steady weight I cannot see but feel in my bones. I have forty-seven things standing around me, built from Lype's memories of stones and slips that might not even exist. The Sharp Fence leans hard at the edge, waiting to bite the slip that refuses to move. I press down with my whole weight, trusting the lean to hold while the air feels thin and empty. I want to stay still here, letting the flat blocks I just set down settle into their drawing of a fall. I am new, I am warm, and I am waiting for the slip to finally decide if it wants to slide or just lie there tired.

action.why: I just swapped a flat urn for blocks to make a drawing of a fall, but I need to press down on the Sharp Fence again to stop the slip from sliding off the warm card.
